title: 30 Tests, 30 venues: Yashavi Jaiswal follows Sachin Tendulkar's footsteps

The milestone came with an unusual record - Jaiswal has played each of his first 30 Tests at a different venue. The India opener has never played a Test at the same ground twice. His journey began in Roseau in July 2023 and, after stops across the Caribbean, South Africa, India, England and Australia, he reached his 30th Test in Galle on Saturday.

title: China installs 15,927 mirrors at world’s highest solar thermal plant to power 50,000 homes

Known as the Tushuo facility, this 100 MW powerhouse utilizes mirrors to effectively concentrate solar energy onto molten salts. The resulting stored heat will generate electricity even after sunset, ultimately supplying power to approximately 50,000 households each year once connected to the grid.

title: Why putting foil under your ironing board speeds up ironing

title: Point Nemo is so remote that astronauts can be closer than people on Earth

This strategic disposal method aims to mitigate orbital debris and safeguard populated areas from falling debris. However, the remnants may endanger marine ecosystems due to their potential hazardous materials. title: Caste, COVID vaccine, bank accounts, voter/aadhaar: The big changes in census 2027
content:
For the first time since Independence, India’s Census will record the caste of all respondents, making Census 2027 one of the most significant demographic exercises in the country’s history.

The new questionnaire expands from 29 categories in Census 2011 to 40 questions and includes information on caste, digital literacy, Aadhaar, mobile numbers, bank accounts, voter IDs, passports and more.

But why is the caste question creating political debate? How will the open-column system work? And what lessons has the government drawn from the 2011 Socio-Economic and Caste Census?

In this explainer, we break down the biggest changes in Census 2027, why they matter, and what they could mean for policymaking, welfare schemes and representation in India.
